sources.entry: Leafy - Look up any word on screen with ⌥A, including in PDFs and images, and save it to a searchable local library. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Leafy
summary.one_liner: Leafy is a Mac vocabulary builder that looks up any word on screen when you press ⌥A and saves words to a searchable local library.
use_cases: Looking up unfamiliar words while reading on a Mac
Translating medical abbreviations in clinical notes
Building a personal vocabulary list while studying
Adding looked-up words to Anki flashcards
Looking up words inside PDFs and images
summary.what_it_does: Leafy lets you press ⌥A to look up any word on screen without switching tabs, and the page says this works in PDFs and images too. Looked-up words are saved to a searchable local library. You can set it to check your own personal word and phrase list first, so custom meanings (for example, medical abbreviations) appear before general definitions. The page describes an Anki integration where Leafy checks your Anki deck first and lets you add a missing word directly to Anki from the popup. The page is mostly a collection of user testimonials, so details beyond these features are not stated.
notable: Press ⌥A to look up any word on screen, including in PDFs and images
Personal vocabulary list checked before general definitions
Anki integration: check your deck and add cards directly from the popup
Saves words to a searchable local library
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page; the awesome-mac listing marks it as freeware, which is the only hint
Page content is mostly testimonials, so few technical details are given
Anki integration depends on configuring settings
